major_features: Inverted index builder with positional postings lists for phrase matching
Custom English Porter Stemmer and tokenizer implementing word normalization
Sparse BM25 scoring engine calculating term frequency and inverse document frequency
Dense vector index using Locality Sensitive Hashing (LSH) for high-dimensional cosine similarity
Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) rank merger with configurable hyper-parameters
On-disk binary serialization layout with CRC32 integrity verification
Boolean query parser supporting nested AND, OR, and NOT operators
Dynamic document update and deletion mechanics updating both sparse and dense indexes in-place
candidate_ideas.name: VeloSearch
candidate_ideas.pain: High latency, complex deployment setups, excessive memory bloat, and mismatched search results when trying to combine semantic vector search with exact keyword matching on local systems.
candidate_ideas.problem: Standard vector databases are heavy and lack integrated lexical search, while traditional search engines require complex external services and fail to provide hybrid retrieval without substantial overhead.
candidate_ideas.solution: A zero-dependency hybrid vector-lexical search engine written in Python 3.12. It features a custom BM25 index, a custom Locality Sensitive Hashing (LSH) dense vector index, and a Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) engine to combine semantic and keyword results.
candidate_ideas.target_user: Data engineers and systems architects building lightweight local search solutions.
candidate_ideas.verification: Deterministic tests verifying index consistency under concurrency, zero-vector search queries, malformed text inputs, and exact RRF rank merging order using seeded random projections.

major_features: Structured concurrency RPC framework using Java 21 Virtual Threads and AutoCloseable scopes
Persistent binary Write-Ahead Log (WAL) with transaction boundaries and CRC checksums
Leader election state machine implementing randomized election timeouts
AppendEntries log replication protocol with dynamic term matching and indices synchronization
Log compaction and snapshotting to reclaim disk space while preserving state
Deterministic local network partition simulator to test split-brain scenarios
State machine replication loop driving an in-memory key-value store
Dynamic cluster membership transition protocol for safe node additions and removals
candidate_ideas.name: HydraRaft
candidate_ideas.pain: Unpredictable network partitions, race conditions in leader elections, and log corruption that is difficult to isolate and test deterministically.
candidate_ideas.problem: Distributed state machines are difficult to debug, and existing consensus libraries are tightly coupled to heavy network runtimes.
candidate_ideas.solution: A zero-dependency single-JVM Raft consensus engine implemented using Java 21 Virtual Threads. It features structured concurrency, a persistent binary Write-Ahead Log (WAL) with transactional guarantees, and a local network partition simulator.
candidate_ideas.target_user: Distributed systems developers and database engineers needing a reliable, lightweight consensus layer.
candidate_ideas.verification: Integration tests simulating network partitions, verifying that only the majority partition commits transactions, and recovering a crashed node's state from the binary WAL.

major_features: Single-file disk volume formatter with block-level allocation bitmap
Inode table manager tracking file metadata, size, permissions, and direct/indirect block pointers
Hierarchical path parser supporting dynamic directory traversal and creation
Write-Ahead Metadata Journaling engine with circular buffer log for atomic transactions
Double-indirect block addressing scheme supporting large file allocations
Hard and symbolic link implementation tracking inode reference counts
In-place file defragmenter optimizing contiguous block layouts
Integrated fsck-like recovery tool diagnosing and repairing inconsistent inode/block states
candidate_ideas.name: ChronosVFS
candidate_ideas.pain: Data corruption during sudden system shutdowns, lack of granular control over block allocation, and complex portable storage isolation.
candidate_ideas.problem: Native operating system file systems are rigid and lack isolated, portable, crash-consistent storage containers for micro-environments.
candidate_ideas.solution: A user-space virtual file system (VFS) implemented inside a single flat binary file. It features a custom journaling engine, direct/indirect block-level allocation, and an integrated recovery utility.
candidate_ideas.target_user: Embedded systems engineers and security tool developers needing isolated, crash-resilient local storage.
candidate_ideas.verification: Deterministic tests writing highly fragmented data, cutting power (aborting the C process) mid-write, and asserting the journal recovers metadata to a valid, non-corrupted state.

major_features: Multi-resource task queue simulator modeling CPU, memory, and I/O constraints
Custom tabular Q-learning engine with adjustable discount factors and learning rates
State-space encoder mapping current system pressure vectors into discrete indices
Dynamic scheduler dispatch loop executing tasks based on agent-selected actions
Exploration-exploitation decay scheduler balance policy (epsilon-greedy)
Feedback reward calculator evaluating task execution latency and resource waste
Binary state persistence system saving and loading the Q-table matrix
Starvation detector that overrides actions to prevent long-running task lockouts
candidate_ideas.name: SynapseSched
candidate_ideas.pain: Manual tuning of scheduling thresholds is error-prone, resulting in high latency spikes and underutilized hardware.
candidate_ideas.problem: Heuristic-based resource schedulers fail to adapt to dynamic, heterogeneous system workloads, leading to CPU starvation and memory bottlenecks.
candidate_ideas.solution: A local, zero-dependency reinforcement learning agent that optimizes multi-resource task scheduling. It utilizes a custom Q-learning algorithm built from scratch to schedule tasks based on live CPU, memory, and I/O feedback.
candidate_ideas.target_user: Cloud infrastructure engineers and systems performance analysts.
candidate_ideas.verification: A deterministic test suite with fixed random seeds, asserting the agent shifts scheduling policy to prioritize memory-intensive tasks when memory pressure is high, and handling malformed/negative task resource definitions.

major_features: Lexical scanner with custom regular expression match engine and coordinate tracking
LALR(1) parser table generator parsing dynamic grammar definitions from scratch
Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) builder with strict static type checking
Intermediate Representation (IR) generator converting AST into Static Single Assignment (SSA) form
Variable lifetime analyzer constructing precise live ranges
Interference graph builder mapping overlapping variable lifetimes
Chaitin's graph coloring register allocator with spill-to-stack heuristics
Optimization pass implementing constant propagation and dead-code elimination
candidate_ideas.name: AuraIR
candidate_ideas.pain: Debugging compiler optimizations is extremely difficult without clear intermediate representations, and manual register management leads to inefficient code.
candidate_ideas.problem: Modern compilers are massive and obscure the mechanics of intermediate representation (IR) optimization and register allocation.
candidate_ideas.solution: A complete compiler front-end and IR generator written in Java 21. It generates its own LALR(1) parsing tables from a grammar, builds an SSA (Static Single Assignment) intermediate representation, and performs register allocation using Chaitin's graph coloring algorithm.
candidate_ideas.target_user: Compiler engineers, systems programmers, and language designers.
candidate_ideas.verification: Tests compiling invalid code structures to verify error-recovery parsing, asserting SSA form correctness (single assignment per variable), and validating register allocation boundaries when virtual registers exceed physical allocations.
